You are Worker B (explore agent). Your job is to gather content judgments for the repository `canada-bot` at `https://github.com/canada-ca/canada-bot`.

You must write a JSON file to `/workspace/manual_canada-bot.json` containing exactly these keys and allowed values (no extra keys, no comments):

{
  "bilingual": "Yes|No|Unknown",
  "readme_clarity": "Poor|Fair|Good|Unknown",
  "security_policy": "Present|Incomplete|Missing|Unknown",
  "issue_response_quality": "Active|Stale|No Issues|Unknown",
  "release_notes_quality": "Detailed|Version-only|No Releases|Unknown"
}

Allowed values are strictly those strings. If you cannot determine a value, write exactly `Unknown`.

Gathering instructions:
1. `bilingual`:
   - Fetch the README. First try `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/canada-bot/main/README.md`. If that fails (404), try `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/canada-bot/master/README.md`. If both fail, try the API contents endpoint for the root README file.
   - Read the first few hundred lines (or the whole file if small).
   - Look for meaningful French content: French words or phrases, French section headers (e.g., "Description", "Utilisation", "Contribuer", "Aperçu", "Guide"), or a clearly marked French translation block.
   - If there is clear, meaningful content in both English and French, write `Yes`. If it is only English, write `No`. If you cannot fetch the README, write `Unknown`.
2. `readme_clarity`:
   - Read the README content.
   - Evaluate whether it clearly explains:
     a) what the project is,
     b) who it's for,
     c) how to use it (installation, setup, examples, running).
   - Write `Good` if all three aspects are clearly covered with reasonable detail.
   - Write `Fair` if some aspects are covered but one or two are missing or vague.
   - Write `Poor` if it's mostly vague, missing most aspects, or just a title.
   - Write `Unknown` if you cannot read the README.
3. `security_policy`:
   a. Check for `SECURITY.md` in the repo root via `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/canada-bot/contents/SECURITY.md`.
   b. Check `.github/SECURITY.md` via `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/canada-bot/contents/.github/SECURITY.md`.
   c. Check `docs/SECURITY.md` via `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/canada-bot/contents/docs/SECURITY.md`.
   d. If not found in any of those locations, write `Missing`.
   e. If found, read the raw content (use the raw URL or decode the API `content` field).
   f. If the file contains real responsible disclosure instructions (e.g., specific contact email, process for reporting, PGP key, or a clear link to a security team with instructions), write `Present`.

# 🤖 CanadaBot
The Pull Request Bot for Anonymous contributions on GitHub!

---
With PRB0t you can make pull request on GitHub by using a `JSON` description of the changes.

Url: `POST`:`https://canada-pr-bot.herokuapp.com/`

Request Sample:
```json
{
  "user": "<github-user>",
  "repo": "<github-repo>",
  "title": "<pull-request-title>",
  "description": "<pull-request-description>",
  "commit": "<commit-description>",
  "files": [
  	{"path": "<file-path>", "content": "<file-content>"}
  ]
}
```

## What can you do with it?

- If you have a static website hosted in github... you could add a button **Edit this page**.
- You can contribute anonymously to the *Internet 🕸*.
- You can upload files.

## Try it!
```
curl -X POST \
  https://canada-pr-bot.herokuapp.com/ \
  -H 'cache-control: no-cache' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "user": "j-rewerts",
  "repo": "trash",
  "description": "🤖",
  "title": "Review this",
  "commit": "a commit",
  "files": [
  	{"path": "README.md", "content": "Bleep bloop."}
  ]
}'
```

Or [try it](https://codepen.io/jrewerts/pen/vYBGVyY) in your browser!

Or [try it](https://www.getpostman.com/collections/e9b9deac7148e7dd0473) in Postman!

### Docker

You can also run PRB0t with Docker! Just run
``` bash
docker run -p3000:3000 -e GH_TOKEN={YOUR GITHUB TOKEN} jrewerts/prb0t:latest
```

## Development

This project uses Node.js and the Micro framework. To get started

1. Clone this repository.

``` bash
git clone https://github.com/canada-ca/canada-bot
```

2. From within the newly cloned repo, install dependencies.

``` bash
npm install
```

3. Set the environment variable `GH_TOKEN` to your accounts personal access token. For more info on PATs, see [here](https://help.github.com/en/articles/creating-a-personal-access-token-for-the-command-line).

###### On Mac/Linux
``` bash
export GH_TOKEN=YOUR_TOKEN
```

4. Run CanadaBot.

```bash
npm run dev
```

## Deployment

Updating CanadaBot is done automatically. Currently, it's hosted in [Heroku](https://dashboard.heroku.com/apps/canada-pr-bot). When `master` is changed, a new deploy is created.

data.text:
Now I have enough information to make my judgments:

1. **bilingual**: I read the README. It is entirely in English. No French content, no French section headers, no translation block. So: `No`

2. **readme_clarity**: The README explains:
   - What the project is: "The Pull Request Bot for Anonymous contributions on GitHub!" and explains how to use PRB0t to make pull requests via JSON.
   - Who it's for: Static website owners, anonymous contributors, people who want to upload files.
   - How to use it: Request sample, curl example, Docker instructions, development setup (clone, npm install, set GH_TOKEN, npm run dev), deployment info.
   All three aspects are covered clearly with reasonable detail. So: `Good`

3. **security_policy**: I checked the raw URL for SECURITY.md and got 404. I also checked the GitHub API and got 403 rate limited, but I can also see from the repo tree page that the root files are: .dockerignore, .gitignore, Dockerfile, LICENSE, README.md, package-lock.json, package.json. No SECURITY.md file exists in root, .github, or docs. So: `Missing`

4. **issue_response_quality**: The repo was archived on Mar 19, 2025. There is exactly 1 open issue: #45 "Archiving and moving to https://github.com/canada-ca/ore-ero-bot" opened by nschonni on Mar 19, 2025. Since the repo is archived and read-only, no new comments can be added. The issue is from March 2025, which is before the cutoff of 2026-01-13. So there would be no qualifying comments. Since the repo is archived, there are no new responses possible. But let me check if I can see the comments on this issue. I should try to fetch the issue comments.

Wait, the repo is archived and read-only. I can see the issue page. Let me check if there are any comments. The issue page shows the issue title but doesn't show comment details in the HTML snippet. I should try fetching the issue comments via API or HTML.

Actually, I can use webfetch on the issue page directly to see comments.

Let me also think about the release_notes_quality. The releases page says "There aren't any releases here" and "No releases published". So: `No Releases`

For issue_response_quality, I need to check if the issue has any comments. Let me fetch the issue page.
